title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1969-03-02
lineage: Multi-track reel master > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a stellar Fillmore run featuring an awe‑inspiring Dark Star, The Eleven and a legendary Other One.
ai_review.review: The lossless sound‑board source is praised as crisp, balanced and virtually flawless, giving listeners crystal‑clear vocals and instrument separation. Musically the show shines with a dazzling Dark Star opener, powerhouse performances of The Eleven and Other One, plus strong renditions of Death Don't Have No Mercy, Feedback and We Bid You Goodnight; only a few jams (St. Stephen, Morning Dew, Doin' That Rag) are noted as weaker. Overall it’s a must‑have recording from one of the peak periods of the Dead.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 5 stars, consistently highlight superb performance and excellent sound‑board quality with only minor, isolated criticisms.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Lossless zip files praised; crisp, balanced mix with clear separation of vocals (Bobby left, Jerry right) and instruments. A few reviewers mention minor 'rude' cuts in a couple of jams, but overall the recording is described as pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The show opens with a telepathic Dark Star that sets a high bar, maintains momentum through powerful mid‑set jams, and closes strong with an epic Other One suite; occasional over‑extended sections slightly affect pacing but the overall flow is exhilarating.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for perfect tone, counterpoint playing on Dark Star, and staying in sync with Phil throughout; described as telepathically beautiful.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted as being on the same wavelength as Jerry, delivering superb bass work across the set.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s keyboard work highlighted as unusually tender and playful, adding a special texture to the performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming described as sublime and one of the finest rock drum performances ever captured.
